description: An undergraduate Computer Science student passionate about Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, and intelligent agent development. Interested in applying emerging technologies to real-world challenges through research and innovation. Contributed to FlameWise AI, an AI-powered research assistant integrating NASA FLEX experimental data, semantic document retrieval, and conversational AI to make microgravity combustion research more accessible.
summary:
FlameWise AI is an AI-powered research assistant designed to make NASA microgravity combustion research easier to explore and understand. It addresses the challenge of understanding how flames behave differently in microgravity by connecting NASA's Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) research with intelligent document retrieval and experimental dataset analysis.

The application analyzes 274 supplied NASA FLEX experimental records and retrieves relevant information from two NASA research documents using semantic search. It offers Dataset Analysis, Document Retrieval, Combined Analysis, and Automatic Selection, supported by Gemini and a LangGraph workflow.

By bringing experimental evidence and scientific documents together in one interface, FlameWise AI helps researchers and learners explore combustion findings more efficiently. It is a research-support prototype, not a certified spacecraft fire-safety system.
details:
1. What We Developed

1. What We Developed

FlameWise AI is a specialized AI-powered research intelligence platform designed to transform how researchers explore microgravity combustion science. By bringing NASA FLEX experimental data, scientific knowledge retrieval, and conversational AI into one integrated system, it turns complex research resources into accessible, evidence-based insights.

2. How It Works

The system uses 274 supplied NASA FLEX experimental records and two NASA research documents.

It processes scientific documents into smaller text chunks, generates semantic embeddings using Sentence Transformers, and stores them in a FAISS vector index for efficient similarity-based retrieval.

Gemini and LangGraph support four intelligent answering modes:

  • Dataset Analysis: Answers questions using experimental data.
  • Document Retrieval: Retrieves relevant information from NASA research documents.
  • Combined Analysis: Connects numerical findings with scientific explanations.
  • Automatic Selection: Selects an appropriate answering approach based on the question.

A Streamlit interface allows users to interact with the research through natural-language questions.

3. Experimental Results and Data Visualization

The supplied dataset contains 274 experimental records and 186 observed extinction outcomes, representing an overall extinction percentage of 67.88%.

4. Key Features and Benefits

  • 4. Key Features and Benefits

FlameWise AI goes beyond conventional question-answering systems by connecting numerical experimental evidence with scientific literature.

  • Unified Research Intelligence: Integrates experimental dataset analysis and scientific document retrieval.
  • Evidence-Grounded Responses: Retrieves relevant research passages to support generated answers.
  • Multi-Mode Intelligence: Offers four answering modes for different research needs.
  • Scalable Architecture: Designed to accommodate additional scientific datasets and research domains.
  • Accessible Scientific Exploration: Makes complex combustion research easier to investigate through natural-language interaction.

5. Technologies Used

Python, Google Colab, Streamlit, Google Gemini API, LangGraph, FAISS, Sentence Transformers, Pandas, and NumPy.

6. Dataset and Knowledge Base

The prototype includes:

  • 274 NASA FLEX experimental records.
  • Two NASA research documents.
  • 614 extracted text chunks in the document knowledge base.
  • A 384-dimensional semantic embedding index using the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model.

7. Future Dataset Recommendations

Future improvements could include:

  • Expanding the dataset with additional NASA FLEX experimental records.
  • Including more fuel types and experimental conditions where reliable data are available.
  • Preserving experimental metadata, measurement units, and source references.
  • Adding data-quality checks and more detailed comparisons across experimental conditions.
  • Evaluating retrieval accuracy and answer reliability against expert-verified questions.

8. Limitations

  • Currently focuses on 274 supplied NASA FLEX experimental records and two research documents.
  • Insights depend on the coverage and quality of available scientific data.
  • AI-generated responses may require verification against original research sources.
  • Further expert evaluation and broader dataset integration can enhance reliability and research coverage.
  • The current limitations provide clear opportunities for future improvement and expansion.

9. Conclusion and Future Vision

FlameWise AI demonstrates the potential of combining AI, scientific data analysis, and semantic retrieval to transform how complex research is explored. Starting with NASA microgravity combustion research, our vision is to expand this approach into a scalable research intelligence platform that supports scientific discovery across broader aerospace and engineering domains.
